item.title: Cowboys vs. Titans: Offensive, defensive impact players in Week 11
item.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images If there’s such a thing as a cakewalk victory in the NFL, this Week 11 matchup with the Tennessee Titans could be it for the Dallas Cowboys. The Titans currently holds the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, and as such, are considered one of the worst teams in the league. That should equate to an easy “W” for the Cowboys. Since there’s no such thing as a guaranteed victory in the NFL, the Cowboys still need to remain vigilant this week and do everything within their power to secure their fifth victory of the season. In order to do that they need everyone to play at their best. Some players have a way of impacting the game more than others, which we’ve identified below. Offense – QB Dak Prescott Okay, it’s somewhat cheating to pick the starting QB as the offensive impact player this week, but that’s exactly what we’re going to do anyway. Dak Prescott should have a huge game in this Week 11 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. The Titans secondary currently ranks dead last (32 nd ) in the league in passing yards allowed (266.9) and No. 4 should be able to pick them apart at will. With the weapons at his disposal, Prescott should be able to slice and dice Tennessee’s secondary. George Pickens could have another big game after last week’s 145-yard, three-touchdown performance and CeeDee Lamb should hit the 1,000-yard receiving mark (currently sitting at 976 yards). Throw in Ryan Flournoy’s clutch catches when needed and Dallas’ aerial attack should be lethal this week. Defense – DB Caleb Downs The last two games have been interesting for Caleb Downs, the Cowboys first-round pick this year. He played arguably the best game of his young career in Week 9 against the Indianapolis Colts, but maybe one of his worst last week against the San Francisco 49ers. Experiencing ups and downs for a first-year player is be somewhat expected, but we believe he will bounce back in a big way this week against the Titans. With Christian Parker losing his playcalling duties we believe No. 13 will be put in better position to play to his strengths in Week 11. Mike Petine will likely have him playing more around line of scrimmage, quite possibly using him as a blitzer more this week than we’ve seen in past weeks. Against a second-year QB and a talent deprived offense, we fully expect Downs to make several impact plays to help secure the “W” for the Cowboys. Who do you have as your impact players for this week?

item.title: Packers should lean on running back Kaleb Johnson after their bye
item.description: GREEN BAY, WI - NOVEMBER 15: Green Bay Packers running back Kaleb Johnson (26) is tackled for a loss during a game between the Green Bay Packers and the Minnesota Vikings on November 15, 2026 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, WI. (Photo by Larry Radloff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The bright spots of the Packers’ Week 10 loss to the Vikings are few and far between, but running back Kaleb Johnson was surely among them. “I thought he did a nice job,” LaFleur said of Johnson’s 10-carry, 42-yard outing. “I liked how he was hitting the hole, running with good pad level, pressing the line of scrimmage. I thought that was a positive performance.” If there’s a big takeaway to be had here, it’s that Johnson should be getting the lion’s share of carries going forward, and probably deserves more snaps, too. Josh Jacobs remains a mystery. He’s on track to return in relatively short order from finger surgery, but a potential suspension still looms like the sword of Damocles. He wasn’t overly effective as a runner in his brief return to the lineup, either. Across three games, Jacobs carried 36 times for just 80 yards, an abysmal 2.2 yards per carry. Even the perpetually disappointing MarShawn Lloyd has managed 2.7 yards per attempt this year. Speaking of Lloyd, even if he’s better than Jacobs this year, he’s obviously not the future or the present at the position. Kudos to him for making it all the way back from his various injury issues over the last couple of seasons, but it’s abundantly clear he can’t get the job done. It’s hard to foresee him improving much even if the Packers make major strides on the offensive line. Chris Brooks, meanwhile, is a solid but limited player. It’s probably better to think of him as a fullback at this point, a latter day John Kuhn who mostly finds his way to the field because he’s not going to screw it up for the Packers in pass protection. And since Pierre Strong Jr. has now been released, that leaves us with Johnson as the last remaining back on the roster, and perhaps the most viable. The big problem with Johnson to this point has been his limited value in the passing game. You can see what the Packers think of him there by just look at his snap usage. He was on the field for 13 snaps against the Vikings and carried the ball on 10 of them. As a rule, they don’t want him catching passes or blocking for Jordan Love. But LaFleur did call out Johnson’s pass blocking as his most notable contribution on Sunday. Johnson stonewalled a blitzing linebacker on a 19-yard completion. “The thing I was most pleased with was one of the protections when we hit [Tucker Kraft], he came across and picked up Eric Wilson on the blitz right in the B gap,” LaFleur said. You don’t have to be a tape grinder to see what LaFleur is talking about . Johnson lines up to Jordan Love’s left on the play, but alertly comes across the formation to pick off Wilson just as he jets past Travis Glover. Love completes the pass

item.title: Chargers first win comes at a price
item.description: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 16: Fans react prior to the game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Los Angeles Chargers at M&T Bank Stadium on November 16, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Chargers are 1-8 going into their Week 11 matchup against the New York Jets at SoFi Stadium. The Chargers can breathe a sigh of relief as they won’t go winless, but they have lost the inside path to the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. In this week’s Reacts poll, 43% of fans said they would be okay if the Chargers didn’t get the No. 1 overall pick. The Chargers would have the chance to trade out of the pick with a team looking to select a quarterback, or they could take someone like Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, which could completely change their offense. In last week’s Reacts poll, the confidence meter to determine whether the team is heading in the right direction, is at 13 percent. It’s a slight step down from the 14 percent mark the team was at last week, but one win isn’t enough to rebuild all of the confidence zapped from the eight-game losing streak to start the season. The Chargers are hoping to win their first home game of the year against the Jets at SoFi Stadium. Kickoff is scheduled for Sunday at 1:05 pm PT. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Indiana football is set for the big trip out west to take on Washington on Saturday afternoon at Husky Stadium in Seattle, Washington. The Hoosiers, 9-1 on the season, are looking to lock up bids in the College Football Playoff and Big Ten Championship Game with games against the Huskies and Purdue on deck. Indiana remains in great shape should it take care of business. Here’s a few predictions for the game: Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android for coverage of the Hoosiers and all your favorite teams! Khobie Martin takes over at RB1 Khobie Martin showed something the running backs room really hasn’t in quite a few weeks and that’s multiple, substantial chunk carries against USC. With Turbo Richard out against Washington, someone’s going to need to take over as the lead back. Lee Beebe Jr. has been reliable this season and helped Indiana beat Northwestern, but Martin really showed what he can do against the Trojans, rushing for 6.8 yards per carry and a touchdown with a long of 37 on the afternoon. Indiana’s had enough trouble in the run game lately even before the injury to Joe Brunner. If Martin can produce in spite of that, he’s the guy in the backfield. Charlie Becker eclipses 150+ receiving yards Throwing the ball to Charlie Becker is, by far and away, Indiana’s best offense right now. If Wilson, who had a few near-misses against USC, has to test that group, I think they come down with one, at the very least. They have won 5 of their last 6, which is impressive considering they made a quarterback change 5 weeks ago. The Volunteers entered 2026 with a massive question mark at the QB position. item.title: Bayern Munich’s Max Eberl has bigger fish to fry than Jesse Marsch
item.description: (Photo by Sebastian El-Saqqa - firo sportphoto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Max Eberl had to wonder what he did to deserve Friday’s headache. Between former FC Bayern CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge criticizing Jamal Musiala’s contract and Canada coach Jesse Marsch taking aim at the club, it was a lot to handle. Still, Eberl has no interest in turning Marsch’s remarks into a public back-and-forth. Asked about the Canada boss’s comments, the Bayern Munich board member for sport made it clear the club will not engage in a war of words. His reply was brief, pointed, and deliberately dismissive. “I heard what he said, but we will not respond to it. Sometimes silence is better,” Eberl told Sport1 (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). That is about as close to shutting the door on a topic as one gets without leaving the microphone. Eberl acknowledged the criticism, but Bayern clearly sees no value in a public response. Whether that is the right call depends on how Marsch’s comments are viewed, yet Bayern’s leadership is content to let them sit without escalating things. In a noisy football cycle, refusing to feed a controversy can make a statement of its own — and Eberl is not giving Marsch any extra airtime. Join the conversation! item.title: What can recent signings tell us about the impending lockout?
item.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 27: Dustin May #21 of the Milwaukee Brewers reacts during the second inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game four of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field on October 27, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images There have only been a handful of signings since the World Series. The Braves have added a reliever, Evan Phillips. There’s been perpetual Braves-linked starting pitcher Sonny Gray getting 55 million dollars over 2 years. Dustin May has been grabbed by the Twins at 52.5 million dollars over 3 years. And Jake Bauers got four years from the Red Sox. Ivan asked us two or three weeks ago how many top 50 MLB free agents will be signed before the impending lockout on December 1st. I guess a pretty low number like many of you. It may pick up soon, holiday or not. Three of the four players I mentioned got more money than was projected by the public sources. Bauers had a lower AAV, but did snag another season. So can these signings tell us anything about the impending lockout? Do we have enough of a sample size? Or does the low number of signings tell us anything? We can only attempt to read the tea leaves and sift through the social media posts from MLB and the players. The signed players getting more money might mean a more favorable result for the players. But then again, each of the signing teams can afford to work around these contracts anyway. Labor strife stinks, y’all.

item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 19: D'Andre Swift #4 of the Chicago Bears carries the ball against the New Orleans Saints during the second half of the game at Soldier Field on October 19, 2025 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images This week, the New Orleans Saints will head to Solider Field to face the Chicago Bears in Week 11 of the 2026 regular season. To break it down, Bill Zimmerman of Windy City Gridiron joins us to preview this weekend’s matchup. NJ: How legitimate are the Bears’ Super Bowl aspirations at this point in the season? Does it feel like this could finally be the year Chicago gets it done? BZ: The Jeffery Simmons trade changed everything as far as I’m concerned. The Bears defense was the reason they weren’t a true Super Bowl contender. Dennis Allen was largely doing it with smoke and mirrors. Yes, he had really effective blitz packages on 3 rd down, but that wasn’t sustainable in the playoffs against great teams. The offense was never a question; the defense was. With Simmons, he’s a multiplier. In just two games, we’ve seen the play improve of every defensive lineman and linebacker around him. If their front 7 can play like this, it will help a banged-up secondary that is the weakest part of the team. No one can guarantee a Super Bowl, but I do think the Bears are on the short list of true Super Bowl contenders this year (and that’s very foreign to write). It’s been a drama-filled week for the Ravens, and they’ll be missing Nnamdi Madubuike, so they need to figure out how to put their heads down and grind out this win to avoid dropping six in a row. item.description: Pakistan have announced their much-delayed central contracts for 38 players, with former captains Mohammad Rizwan and Shan Masood, along with opener Imam-ul-Haq, among the notable omissions from the new list released by the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Saturday. The announcement comes after a considerable delay, with the previous central contracts having expired on June 30. The PCB has introduced a new format-based structure, dividing players into separate Test, ODI and T20 categories, alongside a development category that accommodates the majority of the contracted players. The exclusions of Rizwan, Shan and Imam come amid recent setbacks in their international careers. Shan was recently removed as Pakistan's Test captain, while Rizwan and Imam were sent back home from England during Pakistan's tour, following which the visitors suffered a 3-0 whitewash in the Test series. Former captain Shadab Khan has also seen his status reduced, receiving a contract only in the T20 category. Babar, Salman the only players in Test and ODI category Test captain Babar Azam and Salman Ali Agha are the only two players included in the combined Test and ODI category. ODI captain Shaheen Shah Afridi has been placed in the ODI/T20 category, while Sahibzada Farhan, who led Pakistan in their most recent T20 Internationals, has received a contract exclusively in the T20 category. Among the other notable omissions are all-rounder Aamer Jamal, Saim Ayub, young pacer Akif Javed and spinner Ali Usman. Pacers Khurram Shahzad and Mohammad Ali, who recently toured the West Indies and England, have also been left out. The PCB has awarded contracts to 38 players but has not disclosed the remuneration attached to the individual categories. The newly introduced development category has the largest representation, with 19 players included. item.title: Bruno returns – but Newcastle have far bigger concerns against Arsenal
item.description: Bruno returns – but Newcastle have far bigger concerns against Arsenal Matthias Jaissle says he tried “everything” to convince Bruno Guimarães to stay at Newcastle United in the summer. The German had only just arrived at the club when he was faced with the prospect of losing one of Newcastle’s most important players. His efforts were ultimately unsuccessful and Guimarães will return to St James’ Park on Saturday evening wearing the colours of Arsenal. Much of the build-up will inevitably focus on the Brazilian, but Newcastle need the game to be about far more than their former captain. “We counted on him [Guimarães] as a leader,” Jaissle said ahead of the game. The Newcastle boss has also been made aware by his players of just how important Guimarães was during his four-and-a-half years on Tyneside. “There will be friendships there and respect,” Jaissle added. “They’re professional enough to distinguish that and just focus on what’s needed in these 90 minutes. “Our approach is to give him and his colleagues a difficult 90 minutes.” Newcastle have already produced some of their better performances this season when facing former players. Their displays against Alexander Isak’s Liverpool and Sandro Tonali’s Tottenham were both fuelled by intense atmospheres. Guimarães’ return feels different. He gave Newcastle four-and-a-half excellent years and developed a strong connection with the club and its supporters. He is still likely to receive a hostile reception from sections of the home crowd, but Newcastle cannot rely on that alone to lift them. Those games against Liverpool and Tottenham came during the opening two weeks of the season, when Jaissle and his players were still operating with the momentum and energy of a new campaign. Ten Premier League games later, the mood is different. Heavy defeats at Leeds and Coventry, along with poor performances against Aston Villa and Everton, have raised questions over Newcastle’s direction under Jaissle. There were signs of improvement in the draw with Fulham, but Arsenal will provide a much tougher test. Newcastle also face a difficult run of fixtures. After Arsenal, they travel to Brighton before home games against Manchester United and Sunderland. That makes Saturday important not only because of Guimarães’ return, but because Newcastle need to build some momentum before a potentially defining run of matches. There should already be enough motivation. The Premier League champions are coming to St James’ Park, while Newcastle have also enjoyed memorable recent moments against Arsenal. Their victory over the Gunners in 2023 produced a furious post-match reaction from Mikel Arteta, while Newcastle also beat Arsenal over two legs on their way to the 2025 Carabao Cup final. item.title: Insane college hockey brawl between Michigan-Michigan State breaks out — and leads to six suspensions
item.description: Hockey brawl You could have called this the true Battle for the Paul Bunyan Trophy. The No. 1 Michigan and No. 9 Michigan State hockey teams engaged in a wild brawl during Friday’s game that led to six ejections — three from each team — and 116 penalty minutes being issued. The teams battled all over the ice in the third period, with several players hitting the slippery surface, during the Wolverines’ 5-1 home win. Michigan and Michigan State Hockey full 3rd period fight uncut video pic.twitter.com/ewlIsilom1 — Matt Vierling Visionary (@EddyFan410) November 21, 2026 A hit from Michigan State defenseman and 2025 third-round Rangers selection Sean Barnhill to Michigan forward Nick Moldenhauer ignited the brawl. “Well, (Barnhill) took a two-minute penalty and they didn’t like it, and that happens in hockey,” said Michigan State coach Adam Nightingale, per the Lansing State Journal . “You stick up for your teammate and we’re going to stick up for our teammates. The refs did a great job of handling that.” A Michigan State player also shoved Michigan goalie Jack Ivankovic, per The Athletic, which Wolverines coach Brandon Naurato mentioned after the game. A shot of the Michigan-Michigan State brawl. @Eddyfan410/X He told the outlet he was proud of his players for defending each other. “Their guy jumped the bench and came over towards ours,” Naurato said, per the publication. “Anyone comes around Jack it’s not good.” One extended clip of the brawl featured an announcer mentioning the hit from Barnhill to Moldenhauer right before the referees blow the whistle and a multi-player fight broke out. We have a line brawl in Michigan-Michigan State. Started with a hit from behind from Sean Barnhill on Nick Moldenhauer. Multiple MSU players left the box to join in on it. Jack Nesbitt, Sean Barnhill and others ejected. There will be suspensions. Rare scene in college hockey. pic.twitter.com/yi9ZVQEqIh — Scott Wheeler (@scottcwheeler) November 21, 2026 One Michigan State player dropped his opponent to the ice in the scuffle. After a mini-break, another fight erupted near the Michigan bench that led to all-out mayhem. “Benches are clearing, guys are on the ice wrestling each other, what is going on? Friday’s brawl continues. @Eddyfan410/X The announcer said three Spartans who had been penalized left the penalty box and even the goalies got involved. “It’s one of the biggest rivalries in sports so there’s gonna be a lot of that,” said Michigan forward Jack Nesbitt, per The Athletic. “If anyone goes after (Ivankovic) then it’s game on.” The six players that received ejections face one-game suspensions, according to The Athletic, and the teams meet Saturday in East Lansing.

item.description: Bournemouth’s Eli Kroupi favours a move overseas despite Premier League Interest Eli Kroupi Junior is set to disappoint Premier League clubs by moving abroad when the time comes to leave Bournemouth . The 20-year-old made his senior debut for France during the international break and scored his first goal for his country with a winner against Türkiye. Ornstein reveals Eli Kroupi's transfer preference as Europe's biggest clubs circle The Athletic's David Ornstein has said the world's top clubs are tracking the forward, but Bournemouth have no plans to sell. He added that the Frenchman favours a move abroad over a Premier League transfer, when the time comes to leave The Vitality Stadium. "Kroupi's got much longer on his contract, so there's no massive need to sell in a way that you might consider selling [Alex] Scott," he said. "He's been out injured for longer as well. I think Bournemouth want to make use of him this season and they don't think there chances of recouping significant value will be much worse in the summer. Probably better, actually. "My information on Kroupi is that he would like to move at some point outside of England. You've seen very heavy reporting around PSG and Barcelona. If he continues to show the level of form that he was displaying priot to his injury, the biggest clubs in world football will want him. item.title: Mikey Moore reflects on conquering his nerves after Bundesliga breakthrough
item.description: Mikey Moore reflects on conquering his nerves after Bundesliga breakthrough Tottenham Hotspur loanee Mikey Moore has expressed his relief after scoring his first Bundesliga goal in Friday evening’s 1-1 draw between Bayern Munich and FC Cologne. The 19-year-old Englishman admitted afterward that his prolonged wait for a goal had left him concerned about how he might react when presented with a scoring opportunity. Moore nevertheless displayed remarkable composure in the 12th minute at the Allianz Arena. After initiating an attacking combination involving Linton Maina and Said El Mala, the youngster received the ball back from the latter, rounded Bayern goalkeeper Jonas Urbig, and finished confidently to give the visitors an early lead. The goal represented a significant breakthrough for an attacker whose performances had attracted mounting criticism during his first months in Germany. Moore subsequently came close to scoring again after halftime and contributed to several other promising attacking sequences. Get German Football News awarded Moore its Player of the Match distinction and a 7/10 rating for his efforts against the German record champions. Mikey Moore finally rewards Cologne’s patience The performance came at an important point in Moore’s Bundesliga development. As GGFN reported earlier this month , Cologne head coach René Wagner had continued to defend the Tottenham prospect despite inconsistent performances and several appearances on the substitutes’ bench. Wagner repeatedly emphasized that Moore possessed the necessary attacking qualities to succeed in Germany, suggesting that a single decisive moment might provide the confidence required to establish himself. Moore’s struggles subsequently prompted speculation that Tottenham might terminate his season-long loan during the January transfer window. Get German Football News examined the rumours and the considerable doubts surrounding an early recall following Cologne’s defeat to Bayer Leverkusen. Friday’s performance provided welcome justification for that patience. Moore covered 12.5 kilometres against Bayern, more than any of his Cologne teammates, and contested eleven individual duels. His attacking contributions also demonstrated the potential of a partnership that Wagner has been eager to develop. GGFN first reported on the coach’s enthusiasm for a Moore–El Mala combination in September . The two youngsters have subsequently required time to develop an understanding, but their cooperation against Bayern produced some of Cologne’s most dangerous attacking moments. Sporting director Thomas Kessler praised Moore afterward, emphasizing that the club had always recognized his potential despite the difficulties accompanying his adaptation to German football. The 19-year-old nevertheless acknowledged that one successful performance would not be sufficient. item.description: Former Maple Leafs Employee Throws Current Management Under The Bus. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. item.title: How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊
item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
